previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, along with elevated blood glucose and ketones. She was treated with IV fluids, insulin, and IV Dilaudid for pain, while being kept NPO initially. Her symptoms improved over several days, allowing transition to oral medications and a regular diabetic diet. The abdominal pain was likely related to her chronic gastroparesis or a post-viral gastrointestinal episode, though pancreatitis was ruled out due to normal lipase. Urine culture showed contamination, not infection. She stabilized psychiatrically, accepted oral medications, and was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and close follow-up planned.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ yoF w/ a h/o DMI, chronic pancreatitis and 
borderline personality disorder who presents with nausea, 
vomiting; after running out of insulin needles.
.  
# Chronic Pancreatitis/Abdominal Pain/Nausea/Vomiting: On 
admission patient with typical abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting 
in the the setting of hyperglycemia. Lipase elevated. Symptoms 
thought to be related to pancreatitis. Mild tenderness to 
palpation over the epigastrum, without gaurding or rebound. 
Patient was made NPO, supported with IVF and pain/nausea were 
controlled with IV dilaudid and compazine respectively. 
Eventually patient was transitioned to oral medications and diet 
was advanced. Lipase trended down  and patient discharged with 
PCP follow up.   
.
#. Leukocytosis: Afebrile. No signs of infection. UA negative. 
CXR without acute cardiopulmonary process. White count trended 
down without intervention. 
. 
#. Type One Diabetes: Initially blood sugars in the 400s on 
admission with anion gap. With insuling and IVF anion gap closed 
and blood sugars returned to normal range. During 
hospitalization patient was placed on home regimen with moderate 
blood sugar control.  
. 
#. Peptic ulcer disease: Continued omeprazole. 
.
#. Depression/Insominia: Continued Mirtazapine, Trazodone PRN, 
Zolpidem PRN
